quest.rewards_formatted: Guide to Order x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x2

response.speaker: Moce
response.text: Me? It is as you see. I am busy dealing with the barbarian threat! They have been stepping up their attacks — perhaps they might even have sent spies!

response.speaker: Moce
response.text: This is no trivial matter! Vigilance must be maintained until reinforcements arrive!

response.speaker: Moce
response.text: If there is anything else, please bring it up with my adjutant, citizen.

choices.text: A child, out here on their own...

response.speaker: Moce
response.text: Hmm? A child? Where from? Did some new legionnaire disobey orders and bring their family into the camp again...?

response.speaker: Moce
response.text: *sigh* Dominus Cassiodor is far too gentle with these greenhorns. If this were to have happened three decades prior, a Tribunus would've had a whip out by now...

choices.text: Have there been any suspicious happenings lately?

response.speaker: Moce
response.text: Not at present. That said, the barbarians are akin to cunning beasts. Ever will they strike when your guard has been lowered, for surprise is their greatest weapon!

response.speaker: Moce
response.text: By methods most foul they infiltrate our cities and seek out our secrets. Even the slightest lapse in discipline may lead to catastrophe.

response.speaker: Moce
response.text: *sigh* Thirty years ago, when I followed Dominus Boethius to conquest in the far north, they were but a pack of primitives without any such skill for subterfuge. Where did they learn these tricks?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thirty years ago... Your parents wouldn't even have been born yet...

response.speaker: Moce
response.text: Hmm? What did you just say, citizen? I fear my hearing's been going as I age.

response.speaker: Moce
response.text: *sigh* Time truly is cruel. During the conquest of Bituria, I could hear the barbarians' bells calling them to muster from miles away.

response.speaker: Moce
response.text: Fare ye well, citizen! You may report suspicious people to me at any time!

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: *sigh* I wonder when this war will finally be over...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing up there on the roof?

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Hmmm? I'm monitoring the area for any suspicious barbarian activity, of course! Recently... Wait a moment. How did you get up this watchtower, citizen?

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: *sigh* Whatever, that isn't important. Tribunus Mettius says that the savages' assaults are advancing apace. The latest news is that they might have sent spies among us. We must be on guard.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: But would those brutes really be interested in our remote little city? To the extent that they would go through all the trouble of sending spies?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Meat is meat, no matter how small the portion.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Ah, citizen, you speak true! It seems I must keep to my task. Hmm... Judging by how you spoke, might you be experienced in such matters?

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: In which case, could I entreat you to survey the surrounding area? Should the barbarians have been active, they must have left some trail. Like a wooden sword, perhaps...

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Well now, they *are* savages. Would it be so strange that they would use sticks as weapons?

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: In any case, I am counting on you. Should you discover anything, report back to me — consider it your joyous duty as a Remurian.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: To think that... There can be no mistake. This is one of the barbarians' signal poles, by which they send their vile messages!

response.speaker: Giovanni
response.text: *sigh* I cannot believe that their spies truly have infiltrated our ranks. It seems Tribunus Mettius's fears were not unfounded.

response.speaker: Giovanni
response.text: Once I report this matter to him, I will have discharged my duty.

response.speaker: Giovanni
response.text: You have my thanks regardless, citizen. If not for you, our defenses might have collapsed well before the heathen hordes arrived!

response.speaker: Giovanni
response.text: I will surely mention your contribution when making my report.

choices.text: You said it was a wooden sword just now...

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Have you made any discoveries, citizen?

response.speaker: Giovanni
response.text: Stay safe! Report to me should anything arise!
